title: Graph tab: a sub-tab strip for the inspected chat ([ turns ], its perch runs, [ new run ] with the chat), and every perch run with no chat open
operator_decision:
2026-10-08 (TRACK.md, USER GRAPH DESIGN):
- The graph tab stays in the inspector, with a strip of sub-tabs: [turns], one per run of the chat, then [ new run ].
- One graph is drawn at a time.
- The tab follows the chat the inspector shows.
- With no chat open, the sub-tabs are every perch run.
- TUI look: K text keys, no buttons. Every remote string goes through clean and is drawn as a text node. Periodic reads go through core/lane.js; a person's actions use hubPost/hubGet.
why: Today the tab is a run list plus one picked run for the whole page (runs.js:207 `picked`, index.js:32-42). It knows no chat: start does not send one (runs.js:399-400), and with no chat open the tab is not drawn at all. It is a base tab (registry.js:99-101, global:false at :106), so Right() says 'no pane focused' (app.js:1427-1430).
what:
Registration (no app.js edit):
- At the top of graph/index.js: `rightTabs.add({ name: 'graph', icon: '⋔', component: GraphTab, global: true })`.
- A registered tab with a base name takes that slot in place (registry.js:103-111), and Right() prefers the registered component (app.js:1426). It draws the tab with {s: null, sid: null} when no chat is inspected (app.js:1429).
- app.js already imports graph/index.js (app.js:16).

The strip, in a new graph/strip.js: pure words plus one component that takes props. It replaces the bar (index.js:32-34) and RunList (index.js:39).
- `stripOf({ sid, chatRows, allRows, picked, all })` -> [{ key, label, cls, title, sel }]:
  - With a chat: 'turns', then this chat's perch runs newest first, then 'new'. Only rows with `row.chat === sid` are kept: the page filters as well as the perch, so an older perch that ignores ?chat= shows none of another chat's runs.
  - With no chat: every perch run from the unfiltered list, then 'new'. No 'turns'.
  - STRIP_RUNS = 4 runs are drawn, then `[ all N ]` / `[ fewer ]`. This is the LIST_ROWS precedent (view.js:167, 194). The selected run is always drawn, even past the cap.
- A run's label is `<rid> <state>`, from rowLine (view.js:90-97), with its class.
  - Its title is rowLine's title.
  - With no chat open, the title also says which chat the run was started beside: the chat's title from core/hub.js `list` through label() (hub.js:17, 79) and clean. It reads 'started with no chat open' when the run has no tag, and the bare id when the list lacks the chat.
  - row.chat is untrusted. It is only ever compared with ===, or used to look up a list row, and is never drawn unless it passes chatOk.
- `Strip`: one line that wraps, made of K's (core/ui.js:24-34). The selected one is marked with ▸ and the class gsel.
- RunList and its import are removed from view.js and index.js; no test names RunList. rowLine stays (runs.test.mjs:427-435).
- view.js:249 draws `g.error` raw. It is a tool's own output from the journal (jevrun.js:417 `p.error = call.result.content`; jev_graph's is the one result kept unclipped, jevrun.js:393), or a header quoted from it (jevrun.js:422). It becomes `clean(g.error, 240)`, like every other remote string in the view (view.js:247). GP-c's ChatRunView reuses this branch.

The body (index.js:40-42) is exactly one of:
- TurnGraph({s, sid}) from W3 (graph/turns.js);
- RunView (view.js:236-261);
- NewRun (view.js:200-232), when 'new' is selected.
The services line stays above the strip (index.js:31).

Selection, per chat:
- `picks`: a signal of { [sid or '']: key }. It replaces the page-wide `picked` (runs.js:207) and `currentRid` (runs.js:215); index.js is their only reader (grep).
- A key is one of:
  - 'turns';
  - a perch rid (ridOk, runs.js:55);
  - 'new';
  - a chat-run key `w:<id>:<n>`, matching /^w:[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}:\d{1,9}$/. This shape is reserved for GP-c: pickOk accepts it, GP-a never makes one, and it fails ridOk, so no runs/ path is built from it.
- `pickFor({ sid, stored, items, holder })`:
  1. A stored pick that is still in the strip wins.
  2. Else, with a chat: this chat's own run that holds the browser, else 'turns'.
  3. Else, with no chat: the holder, else the newest run, else null, which draws 'no runs yet' above [ new run ].
  4. A holder chosen by default is stored, so a run that ends stays on screen (today's rule, runs.js:277-278). The auto-pick at runs.js:286 goes.
  5. A stored pick that is absent from the strip is KEPT, never erased: pickFor only chooses what to draw. A default (rule 4) replaces a stored pick only once that chat's list has been read OK (its cache entry has ok true) and lacks it. So a page just reloaded, whose chat list is not read yet, keeps its stored pick and draws it as soon as the list holding it arrives.
- Stored picks other than 'new' are kept in localStorage under `minerva.graph.picks`, at most 64 chats.
  - Every read and write is inside try/catch (the notes stash pattern, notes/store.js:278-295).
  - A page with no storage, or a throwing one, behaves the same apart from forgetting.
  - This is the per-viewer convenience that survives a reload. No pane does: see GP-b.
- `[ new run ]` selects 'new', which shows the form (openForm, runs.js:254-261). The form's [ close ] goes back to the pick from before. A start selects the new run.

The chat's runs, read:
- `chatOk` mirrors sessions::id_ok: /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$/. `chatListPath(chat)` is `runs?chat=<chat>` for a chatOk id, else null. hubPathOk accepts it (api.js:104-109).
- `loadChatRuns(chat, lane = true)` uses `hubPoll(chatListPath(chat), 6000)`, or hubGet after a person's action.
  - It is kept per chat in a map capped at 16 chats: { rows, ok, sentence, at }.
  - rows are filtered by ridOk and by row.chat === chat. A failed read keeps the last good rows.
- `tabChat`, a signal, is set by RunsPane from sid in an effect on [sid]. The tab is not remounted when the chat changes (Right keys it by name, app.js:1428).
  - A change asks that chat's list at once.
  - refresh() (runs.js:447-450) also calls loadChatRuns(true) for tabChat when there is one.
  - With no chat, openTab() asks exactly what it asks today (runs.test.mjs:110-127).
- loadRuns (runs.js:279-289) and the unfiltered poll stay. That list is the no-chat strip, and the holder for formGate, NewRun's [ abandon ] and the notice: the holder problem, option A in RT's notes.
- followRow (runs.js:292-303) patches the row in the chat's cached list too. A run that ends while it is shown then reads ended in the strip without waiting 10 s.

A new run carries the chat:
- The index.js run line becomes `const run = () => R.startFromForm({ chosen: ch, form, acting, holder, chat: sid });`. It is still one line with no health word (runs.test.mjs:518-521).
- startFromForm (runs.js:191-195) passes chat to `startRun(graph, args, chat)`.
  - startRun posts {graph, args, chat} only when chatOk(chat), else exactly {graph, args}. The deepEqual at runs.test.mjs:413 is unchanged.
  - On a 202 whose data.chat is the chat sent: a row { rid, graph, args, state: 'running', chat } goes into that chat's cache AT ONCE and the rid becomes this chat's pick, so the strip holds the new run and draws it before any read returns (today RunView draws the listed row or 'reading the run…', runs.js:401-405, view.js:238). Then loadRuns(false) and loadChatRuns(chat, false); the read replaces the made-up row.
  - A 202 whose data.chat is not the chat sent (an older perch dropped it): the rid is stored as the '' pick (the no-chat view, the only strip that lists an untagged run), NOT as this chat's pick, which goes back to the pick from before 'new'. The notice: 'this perch did not keep the chat on run rN (an older perch?): it is listed with no chat open'.
  - With no chat open, a 202 stores the rid as the '' pick.
  - A 404 {error: 'no such chat'} becomes the notice with the perch's sentence (said, runs.js:64-72).
  - With no chat open, nothing is sent for chat: the run is untagged and shows only in the no-chat view.

The holder from another chat:
- refusalOf (runs.js:198-201) keeps data.chat when it passes chatOk.
- The notice, and the form's holder line (view.js:228-229), add 'started beside <title>' (or 'started with no chat open'), with the title from the hub list through clean.
- NewRun keeps [ abandon ] for a parked holder of any chat: one member, one browser.
- refusalOf puts a `chat` key on the notice only when data.chat passes chatOk; otherwise the key is absent, so the deepEqual at runs.test.mjs:337 is unchanged.

A refusal is drawn where its run is drawn (GP-b's pane included):
- Today answerRun, cancelRun and abandonRun report a perch refusal only through the page-wide `notice` (runs.js:420, 430, 440), and only the tab draws it (index.js:38). A pane on another chat's run would never show it, or the tab would show it under the wrong chat.
- Those three set notice = { text, cls, holder: null, rid }. startRun's refusals keep no rid.
- A pure `noticeFor(n, rid)` in runs.js returns n when (n.rid ?? null) === (rid ?? null), else null.
- RunView (view.js:236) takes a `notice` prop and draws it as one text line under its status line (said() has cleaned it, runs.js:64-72). NewRun takes one too and draws it under its holder line, where its [ abandon ] is (view.js:228-229).
- index.js passes RunView `noticeFor(notice, rid)` and NewRun `noticeFor(notice, holder?.rid)`. The tab-level line (index.js:38) draws only `noticeFor(notice, null)`, still hidden while the form shows its holder.
- One notice at a time, as one action at a time: act() still clears it at the start of every action (runs.js:395), wherever it was drawn.

Under a door (mode() !== 'perch', index.js:46-49): the strip is [ turns ] alone, with a faint 'runs need the perch', over TurnGraph. A saved (kept) chat is offered [ new run ] as well: the tag is only a label.

CSS: strip rules in graph.css, square edges. The strip wraps in the inspector's 30 to 70 cells (graph.css:44).

Docs:
- graph/README.md rows for index.js, runs.js, view.js and strip.js; the picked/'turns' sentence of the index.js row (README:7) is rewritten.
- A tests/README.md row for strip.test.mjs.

Fake perch on PORT=48143, served from GP-a's worktree (its --ui-dir is that worktree's webui/term), with MASTER's perch, fake_eidolon and fake_aoide AFTER RT is merged. The orchestrator rebuilds ~/.cache/minerva-master-target once RT lands; copy the binaries per WAVE3.md.

- FAKE_PERCH_ENV="FAKE_WORKFLOW_CASE=$HOME/.cache/GP-a-live/case FAKE_WORKFLOW_STEP_MS=700".
Curl part (the executor):
- POST /hub/runs with a chat id taken from GET /hub/sessions after a chat exists.
- GET runs?chat=<id> lists only it.
Browser-pane steps (the orchestrator):
1. From the start screen, open two new chats, A and B. On A, the graph tab reads `[ turns ]  [ new run ]` and draws A's turn graph.
2. With `a` in the case file, on A, [ new run ], wiki-hop, start Ancient_Egypt, [ run ]. The strip gains r1, which is drawn, and goes running then done. In the network panel, the POST body has chat=<A's id> and a `runs?chat=<A>` poll appears every 10 s.
3. Focus B: the strip is `[ turns ]  [ new run ]`, with no r1. Focus A again: r1 is still the pick.
4. Write `b` to the case file and start from B. r2 parks and B shows it. Focus A and open [ new run ]: the form says run r2 holds the one browser, started beside B's title, and offers [ abandon ].
5. Close both chat panes. The graph tab, now with no chat, lists r2 (parked) and r1, and each title names its chat. r2 still holds the one shared browser, so a start now would be a 409 (state.rs:530-532, runs/README.md:56): pick r2 and [ abandon ] it first, then write `a` to the case file, then start r3 here (untagged). r3 shows in this view and in neither A's nor B's strip.
6. Reload the page and reopen A: r1 is still A's pick.
7. Widths of 34 and 72 cells: the strip wraps and nothing overflows.
8. The console is clean. Screenshots go to scratch. --stop.
risk:
- Four reads per 10 s while the tab is drawn on a chat, all through the one-request lane: health, the list and the chat's list (plus the shown run's own loop). That is one more than today.
- `picked` goes away: any later slice that read it must read picks instead (only index.js does today).
- The strip must stay short in a 30-cell inspector.
notes: Merge order: W2b-2 is on master (b761462; its graph/ and tests/ files are byte-identical to its worktree, so the line refs here hold). W3 first, because it changes graph/README.md and tests/README.md. W3 does not edit index.js (it reads its chat from props only; TRACK.md W3 launch), so GP-a owns index.js whole. RT before this slice's live check.

Edge cases owned here:
- chat deleted: ?chat= lists [], and its runs stay in the no-chat view.
- a run from another chat: never in this chat's strip; only named in the holder line.
- door mode: no runs, [ turns ] alone.
- a run that ends while shown: followRow, and it stays picked.
The pane's edge cases are GP-b's.
Forks do not inherit their source chat's runs (a fork is a new id); untagged legacy runs show only with no chat open.
